author: Codex

source_artifacts.claim: Authored room defines the upper/lower platforms, four relay pads, reciprocal gates, empty hazard/crate arrays and exits.

prior_knowledge.concept: Separate Isp/Pac lane access and reciprocal partner gates

evidence.claim: Level 11 introduces split colored lanes with reciprocal latches.
Level 10 introduces a powered elevator and distinct role pads.

prior_knowledge.concept: Hold pad versus permanent latch state

evidence.claim: Level 02 distinguishes Isp held door support and Pac rescue latches.

prior_knowledge.concept: Four-stage vertical relay with LINK preserving lift power and opening Pac’s next gate

evidence.claim: Current LINK latch chains the lift to later route access.

mechanics.fact: Isp’s ROUTE latch opens Pac’s lower route. Pac’s LIFT hold powers the lift and opens Isp’s lift gate; if Pac leaves early, lift movement pauses until the pad is held again.

evidence.claim: Pad mode and effects for ROUTE and LIFT.
Early LIFT release freezes carrier; returning resumes it.

mechanics.fact: Isp’s LINK latch preserves lift power, keeps the Isp lift gate open and opens Pac’s link gate; Pac’s HOME latch opens Isp’s home gate.

evidence.claim: LINK and HOME latch effects.

mechanics.fact: A missed lift jump lands on a safe catch shelf with a 70-pixel jump-back route; no hazards or crates are authored. Four collectibles are owner-specific and optional.

evidence.claim: Catch shelf is placed for missed lift jump.
No hazards/crates; four collectibles and two exits declared.
Historical recovery probe walks/jumps back from catch shelf.

legal_routes.name: Four-pad split relay (historical source-level ordinary-input route; feasibility evidence only)

steps.goal: Latch ROUTE to open Pac’s lower route gate.
steps.action: Isp jumps over the upper-start hurdle and reaches the Isp-only ROUTE latch.
steps.expected_feedback: ROUTE latches and opens Pac’s lower route gate.

evidence.claim: Isp-only ROUTE pad opens Pac route gate; source defines upper hurdle.
Historical source route reaches ROUTE first and describes its gate effect.

steps.goal: Hold LIFT so the powered carrier can take Isp to the upper landing.
steps.action: Pac moves to the lower LIFT pad and stays there; Isp boards the lift and rides upward.
steps.expected_feedback: Pac’s held pad powers the lift and opens Isp’s lift gate; leaving LIFT early freezes the lift.

evidence.claim: Pac-only hold powers relay lift and opens Isp lift gate.
Historical report verifies Pac LIFT and source-level motion; early release freezes and return resumes.

steps.goal: Latch LINK to preserve lift power and free Pac to advance.
steps.action: Isp jumps from the lift to the upper landing and reaches LINK.
steps.expected_feedback: LINK latches power, keeps Isp gate open, and opens Pac’s LINK gate.

evidence.claim: Isp LINK latch preserves lift power and opens Pac link gate.
Historical ordinary-input route reaches LINK after lift ascent.

steps.goal: Latch HOME to open Isp’s final passage.
steps.action: After LINK opens the lower route, Pac crosses to HOME and latches it.
steps.expected_feedback: HOME opens Isp’s home gate so Isp may descend toward the exits.

evidence.claim: Pac-only HOME latch opens Isp home gate.
Historical route reaches HOME after LINK.

steps.action: Pac and Isp traverse their now-open routes to the lower-right exits.
steps.expected_feedback: Both heroes can reach their role-matched exits.

evidence.claim: Source defines both exits and the preceding role-specific gates.
Historical ordinary-input traversal reaches both exits.
Route report describes causal pad sequence.
Historical ordinary-input traversal completes with both exits; omitted gates and recovery were separately probed.

isp: Reach and latch ROUTE to let Pac cross the lower gate. Ride the lift while Pac holds LIFT, then jump to upper LINK to preserve power and free Pac. After Pac HOME, use the final open passage to reach exit.
pac: After ROUTE opens the lane, hold LIFT while Isp rides up. Once LINK opens Pac’s link gate, cross to HOME and latch the final Isp passage. Reach Pac’s exit.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac steps off LIFT before Isp has latched LINK.
common_mistakes.consequence: The lift freezes and Isp cannot complete the ascent until support resumes; the route remains unresolved rather than timed out.
common_mistakes.recovery: Pac returns to LIFT to restart the carrier; source route probes verify this pause/resume behavior.

evidence.claim: LIFT hold powers carrier; LINK latch later preserves power.
Historical probe confirms early release freezes and returning resumes.

common_mistakes.mistake: Isp misses the lift or landing jump while Pac is holding LIFT.
common_mistakes.consequence: Isp falls onto the catch shelf; without LINK, the next pad gate remains closed, so Isp must reboard and repeat the ascent.
common_mistakes.recovery: Jump left 70 pixels from the catch shelf back to the upper start, then return to the lift. The source route report verifies this ordinary-input recovery.

evidence.claim: Catch shelf and left return geometry are authored for missed lift jump.
Missed-jump recovery probe passes and describes 70-pixel jump back.

common_mistakes.mistake: Try to bypass a relay gate before its partner pad is latched.
common_mistakes.consequence: The barrier blocks progress; omission probes report ROUTE, LIFT, LINK and HOME each gate the next dependency.
common_mistakes.recovery: Return to the relevant pad and complete the relay; source probes show blocked attempts but no hazard/reset consequence.

evidence.claim: Each pad opens a different next gate.
Omitted-partner simulations remain blocked at the corresponding gate.

optional_collectibles: Isp relay_landing at (865,120), on the upper landing.
Pac relay_lower_hop at (350,450), by lower LIFT.
Pac relay_lower_home at (870,450), by lower HOME.

reasoning.rationale: The route is an ordered four-pad relay: Isp opens the lower lane, Pac powers LIFT, Isp preserves power at LINK, and Pac opens HOME. The task has several dependent steps, though each latch has a clear single effect in source.

evidence.claim: Four pads have a dependent role-specific sequence.
Source route identifies the causal sequence ROUTE→LIFT→LINK→HOME.

cooperation.rationale: Neither hero can complete the relay alone: Pac’s held LIFT enables Isp’s ascent, Isp’s LINK frees Pac, and Pac’s HOME opens Isp’s final passage. This is repeated distinct-role dependency without a narrow simultaneous window.

evidence.claim: Reciprocal role-specific pad effects create successive partner dependencies.
Ordinary route records alternating contributions.

execution.rationale: Both heroes perform several jumps across separated upper/lower surfaces, but the route report demonstrates ordinary-input traversal and missed upper jumps have a catch shelf; no sustained precision evidence supports a higher estimate.

evidence.claim: Hurdle, lift, landing and catch shelf define required jumps.
Historical route and missed-jump catch recovery succeed with ordinary inputs.

timing.rationale: LIFT requires Pac to remain on the pad while Isp rides, but the authored route report verifies a patient wait and says early release freezes the carrier until Pac returns. No active window or deadline is required.

evidence.claim: LIFT is hold-based and LINK latches ongoing power.
Patient traversal and early-release pause/resume are verified; no timed cycle is reported.

hazards.rationale: The room’s hazards and crates arrays are empty, and the source adds a catch shelf for missed lift jumps, so the mandatory route has no authored lethal exposure.

evidence.claim: Hazards and crates are empty; the catch shelf is part of platform layout.
Missed jump can land on catch shelf and recover.

novelty.rationale: Split hero-specific lanes/gates were taught in level 11 and moving-lift roles in level 10; this room adds a taller relay in which Pac temporarily holds power, then Isp latches LINK so Pac can continue. It recombines familiar pieces with a new handoff.

evidence.claim: Level 10 teaches lift/steady/rescue roles.
Level 11 teaches split lanes and reciprocal hero gates.
Current route adds a persistent LINK power/door relay.

recovery_cost.rationale: A missed lift boarding or landing does not reset the puzzle: Isp lands on the catch shelf and can jump back 70 pixels to the upper start; if Pac leaves LIFT early the lift freezes and resumes on return. Retrying is avoidable for documented misses.

evidence.claim: Authored catch ledge sits below missed lift jump.
Historical probes show catch recovery and early LIFT release/resume.

solution_clarity.rationale: The idle canvas shows four role-specific pad names and “take turns,” but not that ROUTE, LIFT, LINK and HOME form a strict ordered chain or that LINK makes lift power persistent; several causal discoveries remain.

evidence.claim: Idle canvas shows ROUTE, LIFT, LINK, HOME and NO POWER labels; no active causal state or sequence is visible.
Source reveals the chained pad effects not established by the idle image.

control_friction.rationale: The runtime defines separate movement keys, but there is no tested paired-human reliability evidence for simultaneous upper/lower coordination; leave friction unknown.

evidence.claim: Distinct key mappings are implementation evidence, not a human control test.

confidence_reason: Source and the detailed historical route report support the four-stage dependency and specific recovery behaviors. The route evidence is source-level/historical rather than first-time human play; clarity and actual two-person execution remain heuristic.

confirmed: The two heroes use separated upper/lower routes and must alternate opening partner-specific DNA gates.
The visible “borrowed glucose” line points toward the lift, but no timed condition was observed; the idle record did not demonstrate the mechanism.
missed_mechanics: ROUTE opens Pac’s lower route; Pac must hold LIFT while Isp ascends; Isp latches LINK to preserve lift power and open Pac’s link; Pac latches HOME to open Isp’s final gate.
The lift is a hold dependency rather than a cycle: early release pauses it, and returning resumes it.
A missed lift/landing jump lands on a safe catch shelf, and all four gates are necessary; source probes block bypass attempts.
incorrect_inferences: The first-pass note questioned whether the central NO POWER region was a lift and what powered it. Source confirms a Pac-held powered lift; no fixed timing window is required.
changed_judgments: Reasoning remains 3 because the four causal pad dependencies are confirmed; the ordered chain is multi-step but each state has a single effect.
Cooperation remains 3 because the room requires repeated alternating contributions from both heroes, without a narrow simultaneous timing window.
Execution remains 2: ordinary-input route has several jumps, but missed lift jumps have a safe return shelf.
Timing changed null→0 because the lift waits on a held pad and can be resumed after release; there is no timed phase to catch.
Hazards changed null→0 because the mandatory room has no authored hazards and missed jump recovery is a catch shelf.
Novelty changed 3→2 because the powered lift and reciprocal split-lane gates were taught in levels 10 and 11; the new element is their extended LINK/HOME handoff combination.
Recovery changed null→1 because the source report verifies reversible fall recovery and pause/resume without restarting the whole relay.
Clarity changed 2→3 because four labels and “take turns” are visible, but the idle scene does not reveal their exact relay order or LINK persistence effect.
unresolved: No human play, deaths, retries, subjective confusion, or control friction were measured.
Historical ordinary-input traces verify route feasibility and specific source recovery probes, not the current campaign journey of a first-time pair.

single_operator_note: One operator would have to switch between lower Pac support and upper Isp traversal, then return to Pac for HOME. This requires divided attention and input switching beyond the two-human baseline; no one-operator performance was measured.
